cohort: 54,045 patients admitted to the Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology in a tertiary care centre for delivery between January 1, 2015 and December 31, 2022
finding: The prevalence of peripartum hysterectomy was 0.074% (95% CI 0.05-0.10), and the major indication was abnormal placentation (62.50%).
mod_finding: The indication for emergency peripartum hysterectomy has shifted in recent years from uterine atonicity to morbidly adherent placenta, likely due to an increase in caesarean section rates.
